title: Hourglass eval scratchpad — quick fidelity probes
content:
Purpose: ad-hoc notes while chasing a weird length-sensitive failure that popped up in nightly smoke. Trying to capture minimal reproducer + an informal rubric for triaging whether this is regression vs config change.

Context:
- Model: rdlw/llamax-13b-v1 -> started seeing higher mute-rate (stops replying) when prompts include >480 tokens + function_call metadata.
- Seen on hosted-prod and local-dedicated repro. Intermittent but more frequent after runtime-kernel update (kernel-select v2.7).
- Quick hypothesis: KV-cache alignment bug when sequence crosses a kernel boundary (long prefix => different kernel path).

Quick checklist (what I ran):
- Repro script (small): replayed 50 samples from nightly sampler (seeded) across 13b v1 vs v1.1 (rolling).
- Enabled token-level tracing for 5 failing runs.
- Toggle: disable continuous batching vs enabled.
- Toggle: quant profile low-precision vs default.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick Triage — 0..3, 0=not observed, 3=clear regression):
- Stop-rate: 0..3 => whether model truncated early (stopped replying).
- Incoherence: 0..3 => output semantically wrong within first 20 tokens after prompt.
- Function-call misfire: 0..3 => model returns wrong JSON shape for function invocation.
- Repro stability: 0..3 => how often repros in 10 runs.

Run notes (selected samples):
1) sample A (seed 142): prompt length ~512 tokens, includes function schema metadata.
>>> PROMPT: user asks to summarize logs and call `extract_errors()` with args.
<<< V1 (13b v1): "{\"name\": \"extract_errors\", \"args\": {\"errors\": []}}"  <-- function call returned empty despite visible errors in logs. Score: Stop-rate=1, Incoherence=1, Function-call misfire=2, Repro stability=2
<<< V1.1 (13b v1.1): full textual answer + correct function call. Score: Stop-rate=0, Incoherence=0, Function-call misfire=0, Repro stability=3
Notes: v1 often emits function call with empty list; v1.1 unaffected. Suggests generation policy/regression in system prompt handling or RNG seed change.

2) sample B (seed 321): prompt length ~380 tokens, many bullets.
>>> PROMPT: rewrite bullets into brief executive summary.
<<< V1: replies but drops last bullet content repeatedly. Score: Stop-rate=2 (truncated), Incoherence=1, Function-call misfire=0, Repro stability=1
<<< Local-dedicated with batching disabled: works fine. With batching enabled: failure.
Notes: points to batching + kernel interplay.

3) sample C (seed 980): short prompt, triggers hallucinated function call fields (extra nulls). Only seen on quant-profile-low.
Score: Function-call misfire=3 for quant-low, 0 for default.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
- 1) Batching path + kernel boundary misalignment causes early termination or truncated KV state. (high)
- 2) Kernel-select v2.7 regression with long-prefix handling (med-high)
- 3) Quant profile interaction with JSON emission logic (medium)
- 4) Upstream system prompt change that reached only v1 hosts (low)

Quick experiments to run (next 48h):
- A: Replay failing sample set with batching turned off (on prod and dedicated) — confirm reduction in failure.
- B: Run with kernel-select pinned to v2.6 on a dedicated node, compare.
- C: Narrow down prefix length at which failure starts (binary search 320..560 tokens). Log tokenization boundaries.
- D: Run with deterministic sampling (fixed RNG) to see if randomness affects empty-list function returns.

Notes to FYI collaborators:
- Evan: saw same empty-list behavior on your recent canary logs? Put pointer to GH PR and traces.
- Rina: can you cross-check if any system prompt changes touched function_call scaffolding around the release window?

Misc short-term fixes (if we confirm batching bug):
- temporary mitigation: disable continuous batching for routes >= 400 tokens for 13b-v1 family (config flag).
- longer term: kernel-select fallback that forces single-kernel execution when long-prefix + function_call detected.

Open questions / weird artifacts:
- Why does quant-low only affect function-call shapes and not plain text truncation? Might be timing/latency leading to early flush.
- Token traces show a stray EOF token at boundary in 6/8 failing runs — what stage inserts EOF?

To capture before I forget (TODO):
- Save 20 failing traces to GH pr as artifacts (trace ids list).
- Draft short repro script for infra to run on dedicated (one-liner).
- Add small unit test in replay-toolkit to simulate long-prefix + function schema outputs.

End quick log. Leaving this as a personal scratchpad — will formalize into an issue if A/B repro confirms.

Small sign-off note: sleep deprived hacky notes, expect gaps. If anyone picks up, ping me @maya on Slack and reference JIRA INF-981.
